title: On Murmurations: the Lipschitz bound for the Chebyshev-type polynomial at a fixed base point (Lemma 2.9)
author: Timothy Nelson, Erick Ross, Maya Wassercug, Hui Xue
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's Lipschitz bound for the Chebyshev-type polynomial at a fixed base point, printed as Lemma 2.9 (source0.tex lines 709-715) and delivered with the paper's own complete 86-line proof (lines 716-801). The statement bounds the oscillation of U_{K-1} between two points of the interval by a constant times K over one minus the modulus of the base point, uniformly over all integers K and all base points inside the open interval, with the endpoint cases included. The proof is the paper's own argument: it writes the polynomial through its trigonometric form, converts the difference into a sum of cosine terms, splits the summation according to whether the angle increment is small or large, estimates the two regimes separately with the mean value theorem and a geometric-series bound, and combines them into the stated constant. This is a research-level analytic estimate used in the paper's study of murmurations rather than a qualifying-examination exercise, so the unit is H2. Delivered with the paper's own proof, in the paper's own notation, as the single primary proof body; the unit is H2.
